correctness.rationale: The symmetric Markov kernel yields exact crossing mass for each unit jump. The beta-binomial tail identity converts it to independent binomial absolute differences. A positive derivative 2m P(S_{m-1}=0) with respect to u=s(1-s) proves strict midpoint optimality, and telescoping at s=1/2 produces the central binomial factor. The BV signed-jump decomposition extends the bound to all distributional BV and forces equality at a centered jump. An exact polynomial/binomial checker confirms n=0..15 and further tests; finite experiments are not the proof.

value.rationale: A natural sharp norm for integrated approximation of BV discontinuities is evaluated for all polynomial degrees and all real BV inputs, including rigid equality. It identifies an exact, reproducible binomial kernel-mixing penalty with leading factor sqrt(2) compared to point-sampled Bernstein smoothing; pointwise convergence and variation diminution alone do not supply this design calibration.
